answer: Renewal is the gate: every annual licence costs a base fee multiplied by the number of licences live, so the price of staying is set by the crowd. A lone agent on the ridge pays the base and no more, but a farm inflating the register to k names raises the multiplier for each of them, and its total bill before the first renewal clears runs to base times k squared over two. Splitting across wallets changes nothing, since the register counts identities, not keys. When the fee at the nadir of the curve exceeds an epoch's payout, the gale of clones is priced out and honest renewal stays cheap.
